subject: mathematics
title: Point Detective Review
objective: Recognize and describe points, lines, line segments, rays, and special line relationships.
introduction: Kite strings make different kinds of paths. Can you use endpoints and arrows to tell them apart?

vocabulary.definition: An exact dot on a paper or screen that marks a specific location.
A straight path with two definite endpoints that stop.
A straight path with one starting point that goes on forever in one direction.
A straight path with no endpoints that goes on forever in both directions.

activities.instruction: Watch how endpoints and arrows identify the road figures.
activities.content: A dot marks one location. A segment stops at two endpoints. A ray starts at one endpoint and continues with an arrow. A line has no endpoints; parallel lines stay apart, while perpendicular lines meet at a right angle.

items.prompt: Which of these marks one exact location?

options.text: a long straight path that never ends
a wavy curve with no endpoints

items.explanation: A point marks one exact location. A curve, a number sentence, and an endless path do not.

items.prompt: Which of these has two endpoints?

options.text: a wavy curve with no endpoints

items.explanation: A line segment has two endpoints. A ray has one, and a point has none.

items.prompt: Which of these has one endpoint and goes on in one direction?

options.text: a long straight path that never ends

items.explanation: A ray has one endpoint and continues in one direction. A segment has two endpoints, and a line has none.

items.prompt: Which pair of lines never meets, no matter how far they go?

options.text: perpendicular lines that meet at one point

items.explanation: Parallel lines stay the same distance apart and never meet. Perpendicular and intersecting lines do meet.

items.prompt: On Milo's garden map, point A marks a spot. Which statement about points and lines is true?

options.text: a line has exactly one endpoint
a segment goes on forever in both directions

items.explanation: A point marks one location. A line has no endpoints, a ray has one, and a segment has two.
